newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Guterres dismisses EMU competitivity fears.
newsitem.headline: Guterres dismisses EMU competitivity fears.

text.p: Prime Minister Antonio Guterres dismissed on Wednesday suggestions that Portugal could suffer inside a single currency if economic competitors such as Spain and Italy were left out.

Guterres, who reaffirmed his commitment to being in the first wave of European Union members to unite in monetary union, said that concerns about competitive devaluations by countries on the outside were totally unfounded.

Speaking to the Portuguese Industrialists Association, Guterres said that the European Union would have accords that blocked such action by states that did not qualify or preferred to delay joining a single currency immediately.
"The move is towards making sure such things are not viable," he said in a speech.
Guterres said that being part of the 'hard core' that set up Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999 could only be positive for Portugal.
The government was determined to put Portugal within limits set down for EMU membership for both the budget deficit and inflation in 1997.
Portugal's determination to be amongst the EMU pioneers had already brought benefits in the form of greater credibility for the country's economy and lower interest rates, he said.
He noted that the interest rate differential with Germany, which had been 4.5 percentage points when he took office last November, had fallen to 1.6 percentage points.
